being worshiped appropriately by the blessed ones residing there, / the twice-born, unobstructed there, entered the inner chamber.
Having entered that spotless celestial chariot resembling the sun, / he saw the husband of Kamalā resting on a serpent couch,
his two feet being gently massaged by Lakṣmī's lotus hands. / Seeing him, Bhṛgu, the tiger among sages, filled with rage,
kicked his left foot onto the splendid chest of Viṣṇu. / Rising up swiftly, the Lord, saying with joy, "Blessed am I!"
joyfully pressed his foot with both hands; / gently massaging that foot, he spoke sweet words:
"Blessed am I this very day, O brahmin sage; I have accomplished my purpose for all time. / From the touch of your foot, auspiciousness will be upon my body.
They are the cause for attaining all prosperity; comets to the arisen host of calamities; / bridges across the boundless ocean of worldly existence—may the dust of a brahmin's feet purify me!
On whose body the dust of a brahmin's feet remains always, / on him abide all holy sites such as the Gaṅgā, without doubt."
Having said this, Janārdana quickly rose up together with the goddess / and worshipped [him] with devotion using divine garlands, sandal paste, and other offerings.

Seeing him, the tiger among sages, filled with joy and with tears in his eyes, / rose from the best of seats and bowed down to that ocean of compassion; / folding his hands together in reverence, the one of great austerities said with joy:
The venerable Bhṛgu said: / Ah, what form! Ah, what peace! Ah, what knowledge! Ah, what compassion! / Ah, what entirely spotless patience! Ah, the quality of sattva in Hari!
Natural and auspicious is the sattva of that ocean of virtues; / no such thing exists at all in any of the other dwellers of heaven.
You alone are benevolent to brāhmaṇas and a refuge, Puruṣottama; / you alone are the lord of brāhmaṇas, no other god is ever to be worshipped.
Those who worship other gods instead of you, Puruṣottama, / have fallen into heresy and are despised by all the world.
For brāhmaṇas who know the Veda, you alone are the object of sacrifice, Janārdana; / no one else among the gods is ever to be worshipped.
Brahmā, Rudra, and the rest are not to be worshipped, being mixed with rajas and tamas; / you, possessing the quality of pure sattva, are to be worshipped by the twice-born.
The water of your feet should be served by the ancestors and the dwellers of heaven, / and by all earthly gods; it grants liberation and removes sins.
The remnants left over from what you have eaten / should indeed be enjoyed by the ancestors, the dwellers of heaven, and earthly gods, but never by others.
The food, flowers, and water of the other gods, / all their remnants of worship are untouchable, being equal to liquor.
Therefore indeed, having worshipped the eternal one, a wise brāhmaṇa / should constantly partake only of your holy water and your tasted food.
A brāhmaṇa should neither look upon another god nor worship him; / he should not eat the grace-offering of another, nor enter the sanctuary of another.
Whatever brāhmaṇa here does not give to the ancestors in the ancestral rite / the food and water tasted by you, all that becomes fruitless.
For thousands of millions of kalpas and hundreds of millions of kalpas, / his ancestors fall into the hell of pus and blood.
Whoever sacrifices or gives what has been offered to you, O Lord, / the satisfaction of the deities and ancestors attains eternity.
Therefore, you alone are to be worshipped by brāhmaṇas; there is no one else. / Whoever out of delusion worships others will become a heretic.
For you are glorious Nārāyaṇa, eternal Vāsudeva, / Viṣṇu, all-pervading, eternal, the supreme Self, the Great Lord.
You alone, benevolent to brāhmaṇas, possessing pure sattva, are to be served by brāhmaṇas; / because you are the object of worship for brāhmaṇas and also because of your quality of pure sattva,
reach the status of brāhmaṇas among all the gods; / for brāhmaṇas always worship you alone, Puruṣottama.
They became your brāhmaṇas and none others; there is no doubt about that. / Benevolent to brāhmaṇas is the son of Devakī; benevolent to brāhmaṇas is Madhusūdana;
benevolent to brāhmaṇas is the lotus-eyed one; benevolent to brāhmaṇas is Viṣṇu, Acyuta; / benevolent to brāhmaṇas is the blessed Kṛṣṇa, Vāsudeva, Acyuta, Hari;

6.255.s:
brahmaṇyonārasiṃhaḥ syāttathā nārāyaṇo'vyayaḥ
brahmaṇyaḥ śrīdharaḥ śrīśogoviṃdovāmanastathā
6.255.d:
ब्रह्मण्योनारसिंहः स्यात्तथा नारायणोऽव्ययः
ब्रह्मण्यः श्रीधरः श्रीशोगोविंदोवामनस्तथा
6.255.m: benevolent to brāhmaṇas is Nārasiṃha, and so too the imperishable Nārāyaṇa; / benevolent to brāhmaṇas is Śrīdhara, the Lord of Śrī, Govinda, and likewise Vāmana;
benevolent to brāhmaṇas is Yajñavārāha, Keśava, Puruṣottama; / benevolent to brāhmaṇas is the glorious Rāghava, Rāma, the lotus-eyed one;
benevolent to brāhmaṇas is Padmanābha, and likewise Lord Dāmodara; / benevolent to brāhmaṇas is Mādhava, Yajña, and likewise Lord Trivikrama;
and benevolent to brāhmaṇas is Hṛṣīkeśa, the yellow-robed Janārdana. / Obeisance to the god benevolent to brāhmaṇas, to Vāsudeva who bears the bow Śārṅga;
to Nārāyaṇa, to the Lord of Śrī, and to the lotus-eyed one. / Obeisance to the god benevolent to brāhmaṇas, to Vāsudeva, to Viṣṇu;
obeisance to you, the supreme Self, full of auspicious attributes. / Obeisance to the god benevolent to brāhmaṇas, whose form is all gods;
to the one whose form is the Boar, the eternal lord of the three Vedas, obeisance to you! / Obeisance to the god benevolent to brāhmaṇas, who reclines on the serpent bed;
to the one with eyes like lotus petals, to Rāghava, obeisance, obeisance! / Deluded by your illusion, all the gods and sages
do not know the great Self, the Lord of all the worlds, O Master; / they do not know you, O Blessed One, even though they know all the Vedas.
By his names, forms, qualities, Lord of Śrī, and by actions even if sinful, / who is capable of knowing your sattva that indicates supreme transcendence?
Sent by the great sages, I have come to your presence / to know your character and qualities, Keśava, my foot
was placed upon your chest, Govinda; that should be forgiven, O ocean of mercy! / Having spoken thus, Bhṛgu, bowing repeatedly to the god,
revered there by the divine, great-souled great sages, / went back, joyful at heart, to the sacrificial ground named Śubhā.
Seeing that great-souled one arrived there, the great sages / rose to greet him, paid homage, and performed worship according to rule.
The eminent sage reported all that to them: / 'The two best among gods, Brahmā and Īśāna, are overwhelmed by the qualities of rajas and tamas.
They were cursed by me; they are not to be worshipped by brāhmaṇas, O best of sages. / One who has fallen into unfriendliness to brāhmaṇas has taken a contemptible form;
Śaṃkara, enveloped in tamas, was cursed on the peak of Kailāsa. / Viṣṇu is made of pure sattva, an ocean of auspicious attributes;
Nārāyaṇa is the supreme Brahman; Hari is the deity of brāhmaṇas; / benevolent to brāhmaṇas is the husband of Śrī, Viṣṇu, Vāsudeva, Janārdana;
benevolent to brāhmaṇas is the lotus-eyed one, Govinda, Hari, Acyuta. / He alone is to be worshipped by brāhmaṇas, and no other, O best of men!
Whoever out of delusion worships another will become a heretic. / Merely by remembering Kṛṣṇa, there is liberation even for sinners.
The water of his feet is to be served, and the remnants of what he has eaten are purifying, / granting heaven and liberation to men, and especially to brāhmaṇas.
One should always offer the oblation presented to Viṣṇu to the gods, / and one should give that very same to the ancestors; it all attains eternity.
Whatever twice-born does not give what was eaten by Hari to the ancestors in the ancestral rite, / his ancestors constantly eat feces and urine.
Therefore, the grace-offering of Viṣṇu alone should be consumed by the twice-born; / but the floral remnants of other gods are contemptible.
If a brāhmaṇa weak in knowledge partakes even once / of the floral remnants of Śaṃkara and others, he certainly becomes an outcaste.
For thousands of millions of kalpas he is cooked in the fire of hell. / The floral remnants of Rudra and the other dwellers of heaven, O best among the twice-born,
are considered food of rākṣasas, yakṣas, and piśācas, equal to liquor and meat. / The oblation consumed by [such] gods is not to be eaten by brāhmaṇas.
Therefore, abandoning all others, worship only eternal Viṣṇu / unwearied for as long as you live, O best among the twice-born!
Regarding that supreme abode of Viṣṇu with doubts dispelled, / endowed with the five rites of purification beginning with brand-marking, with auspicious minds,
worship thoroughly the non-material Hari, O best among the twice-born! / Brāhmaṇas whose arms are marked with the discus become non-material and auspicious;
those lacking the mark of the discus, however, are called material and tāmasic. / Therefore, as a destroyer of the flood of sins born of contact with the material,
one should bear the heated discus and conch of Hari on the bases of the arms, / and wearing the vertical forehead marks upon one's limbs according to the prescribed scriptural path,
one should worship Puruṣottama according to the rules with the jewel of mantras, / and one should constantly and unweariedly render service to his grace-offering.'
In the worship of his surrounding deities, one should always worship the gods. / Knowing him alone to be the supreme Lord, the enjoyer of all sacrifices,
one should continually offer oblations, give gifts, and chant, O twice-born!
Vasiṣṭha said: / Addressed in this manner, all those sages, their sins diminished, / bowed properly to Bhṛgu and then said with folded hands:
The sages said: / "O venerable one, dispeller of doubts! You alone are the best of the twice-born. / O holy one, you are the refuge of the world, you are the supreme goal.
You alone are the supreme dharma; you alone are the supreme austerity. / By your grace, O Brahmin, we shall indeed attain [it] and not otherwise."
Vasiṣṭha said: / Having thus praised the Brahmin Bhṛgu, all the great sages, / having received the mantras from him, worshipped Acyuta.
All this has been recounted to you incidentally, O best of earthly rulers! / Indeed, by the touch of Rāma's lotus-hand, O best of kings,
that form of his, censured by the world, will become spotless. / Rāghava is the purifier of all the gods, the supreme Puruṣa.
Touched and seen by him alone, Śaṃkara and the others became spotless. / Janārdana is the father and mother of all the gods,
the protector of all the worlds, an ocean of maternal tenderness. / Go to him alone for refuge, if you desire the supreme abode.
All this Purāṇa, equal to the Vedas, has been recounted to you, / which was spoken by Brahmā, O king, in the interval of Svāyambhuva Manu.
To one humble through devotion to Viṣṇu, whose essence is pure, and not otherwise, / to him one should continually proclaim it; that narrative of Hari brings liberation.
Let the reciter be a man adorned with the conch, discus, and upward mark; / let it be heard continually from his mouth. You will obtain a son, and not otherwise.
Whoever proclaims this continually, or reads it with concentrated mind, / for him exclusive devotion to the Lord of Śrī arises at all times.
One seeking knowledge obtains knowledge; one seeking righteousness attains righteousness; / one seeking liberation obtains liberation; one seeking desire obtains happiness.
On the twelfth lunar day, on the constellation Śravaṇa, on Sunday, at a solstice, and likewise at an eclipse, / on the new moon and the full moon, one should read it endowed with devotion.
Whoever, with concentrated mind, reads even half a verse or a quarter of a verse / obtains the fruit of a thousand horse sacrifices, without a doubt.
Thus this secret Purāṇa in the form of a collection has been related. / Worship Hṛṣīkeśa if you desire the supreme abode.
Sūta said: / Thus addressed by his guru Vasiṣṭha, that best of kings, / bowed to his guru, worshipped him according to propriety,

and having received the mantra in accordance with the rule from that best of the twice-born, / worshipped Hṛṣīkeśa tirelessly as long as he lived; / in due time he reached the eternal abode of Hari, accessible to yogins.

7.0.s:
atha śrīpādme mahāpurāṇe saptamaṃ kriyākhaṃḍaṃ prārabhyate
lakṣmīnāthapadāraviṃdayugalaṃbrahmeśvarādyāmaraśreṇīnamraśirolirolimāamalaṃ
7.0.d:
अथ श्रीपाद्मे महापुराणे सप्तमं क्रियाखंडं प्रारभ्यते
लक्ष्मीनाथपदारविंदयुगलंब्रह्मेश्वराद्यामरश्रेणीनम्रशिरोलिरोलिमाअमलं
7.0.m:
Now the seventh, the Kriyākhaṇḍa, is begun in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa.

The lotus-pair of the feet of Lakṣmī's lord, spotless with the row of bees that are the bowed heads of the gods headed by Brahmā and Īśvara,

7.1.m:
which nourishes most abundant beauty in the ponds that are the minds of yogins, / which bears a collection of drops of the nectar of Gaṅgā's water, dispelling the misery of saṃsāra;

the Lord who, assuming many forms, protects the entire universe, / devoted to worshipping whose feet they do not plunge again into the world's
the Lord whose abode is continually in the lotus-hearts of all living beings: / homage to that God Hari, who assumed the lovely form of a boar!
That God who, having drawn out all dharmas from the Vedas, proclaimed them in the Purāṇas / in the form of Vyāsa for the welfare of the world: I revere him together with Kamalā.
Once all the sages, desiring the welfare of all the world, / held a delightful assembly in the lovely Naimiṣa forest.
At that moment, the disciple of Vyāsa, of great splendour and renowned, / Sūta, accompanied by hosts of disciples, arrived, remembering Hari.
Seeing that Sūta arriving, who had gone to the end of the scriptures' meaning, / all the ascetics, Śaunaka and the others, stood up and bowed.
He too, the foremost of those who know all dharma, immediately with devotion / bowed down on the ground like a staff to those sages, the supreme Vaiṣṇavas.
On an excellent seat given by those best of sages, that sage of great intellect / sat down in their midst, surrounded by all his disciples.
To Sūta, who was seated there, the best of sages, Śaunaka, / with folded hands and filled with modesty, spoke these words:
Śaunaka said: / "O great sage, Sūta, all-knowing one! When the Kali age has arrived, / by what means, O venerable one, can abundant devotion arise in men?
In the Kali age, all people will be devoted to sinful deeds / and destitute of Vedic knowledge. How can there be welfare for them?
In the Kali age, life-breaths reside in food; likewise, people have short lifespans; / they will be impoverished and afflicted with various sufferings.
In the scriptures, meritorious action is prescribed as achievable through effort, O twice-born; / therefore, in the Kali age, hardly anyone will perform meritorious deeds.
When meritorious actions have perished and sinful action has commenced, / all those of evil intention, along with their lineages, will go to destruction.
By what means, O best one, with little effort, little wealth, and little time, / great merit may arise, tell that indeed, O son of Sūta!
A mortal by whose instruction people perform merit or sin / becomes a sharer in that; so it is determined in the scriptures.
One who instructs in merit, one who is compassionate, one who is free from deceit, / and one who opposes the path of sin: these four are like Keśava.
Having obtained knowledge in this world, he who does not give it to others, / to him Hari, who is embodied as knowledge, does not look with favour.
The man who brings satisfaction to others through the jewels of knowledge and through gems, / that wise man is truly to be known as Hari bearing human form.
You alone, O tiger among sages, have mastered the Vedas and their auxiliary limbs; / indeed, there is no other speaker except you, since you were instructed by Vyāsa."
Sūta said: / "Blessed are you, O best of sages! You alone are the foremost of Vaiṣṇavas, / since you always desire the welfare of all people.
Listen, O Śaunaka! I will speak what you have wished to hear, / for the sake of the welfare of all the world, especially of Vaiṣṇavas.
Listen to that which [Vyāsa] spoke when questioned in full by Jaimini: / the great sage named Jaimini was always engaged in the practice of yoga.
Bowing his head to Vyāsa, that best of sages asked: / Jaimini said: 'O venerable one, knower of all dharma, Vyāsa, son of Satyavatī!
From what can liberation come in the Kali age? Explain that to me from its foundation.' / Sūta said: Having heard Jaimini's words, Vyāsa, satisfied in mind,
began, O tiger among sages, the auspicious narrative. / Vyāsa said: 'O Jaimini, tiger among sages! Blessed are you, O great-minded one!"
Because you always desire to hear the account of Nārāyaṇa. / Whosoever’s intellect turns toward hearing noble accounts,
unto each such person knowledge will arise; knowledge, they say, bestows liberation. / The sinner on earth who takes no delight in an account of Viṣṇu,
the earth was burdened by the Creator with having created him entirely in vain. / The world is praised by Vaiṣṇavas for recounting [Hari's] story;
he who speaks of that [story] as if it were false is to be known as the foremost of sinners. / On whatever day, O best of sages, the account of Hari is not heard,
that day I consider an ill-omened day; a day overcast with clouds is not an ill-omened day. / On whatever part of the earth a story of Viṣṇu takes place,
the Lord never abandons His presence there. / Any man who creates an obstacle at the commencement of a Vaiṣṇava story,
the Lord curses him and departs together with the deities. / Those people who rejoice upon hearing the majesty of Vāsudeva,
they alone are to be known as portions of the gods, worthy of worship and sight, the best of men. / But those who indeed mock upon hearing the majesty of Nārāyaṇa,
they are to be known as portions of the Dānavas, men bound for hell. / All the sacred fords, the Gaṅgā and others, O best of the twice-born,
and the divine seers, the gods, and the sages rich in asceticism [are present] / where the account of Nārāyaṇa, which destroys the disease of sin for crowds of listening folk,
takes place every day. / O sage, listen to the Kriyāyogasāra, rich in meaning and destructive of sin,
accompanied by the account of Nārāyaṇa, together with legendary history."
